title: Grade 4 HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — Mock Exam #3

pages.quiz:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — MOCK EXAM #3
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why is water needed by all living things? (1 mark)
   A. It is always warm
   B. Life cannot continue without it
   C. It makes things noisy
   D. It hides the sun

2. Which of these is one of Parshvanath's four rules? (1 mark)
   A. Take what you like
   B. Wealth at any cost
   C. Be proud
   D. Satya, always speak the truth

3. How should we treat a scripture? (1 mark)
   A. With cleanliness and respect
   B. By sitting on it
   C. By throwing it
   D. By writing on it

4. Which Jain scripture gives advice on a disciplined life? (1 mark)
   A. Ramayan
   B. Dhammapada
   C. Uttaradhyayan Sutra
   D. Sigalovada Sutta

5. Who wrote the Ramayan in Sanskrit? (1 mark)
   A. Guru Nanak
   B. Guru Arjan Dev
   C. Sigala
   D. Sage Valmiki

6. What promise lesson do we learn from the Ayodhya Kaand? (1 mark)
   A. Promises are for kings only
   B. Keep your promises
   C. Forget promises
   D. Break promises

7. How should we say the Gayatri Mantra? (1 mark)
   A. While eating
   B. Shouting
   C. Slowly and clearly, sitting quietly
   D. While running

8. How should you dress to visit a Mandir? (1 mark)
   A. Modestly
   B. Very informally
   C. Wearing school uniform
   D. Wearing a heavy coat

9. What could you use to map the Mandirs in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. A random guess
   B. A safe digital map with a teacher's help
   C. A dream
   D. A song

10. What does pita mean in the prayer? (1 mark)
   A. Wealth
   B. Mother
   C. Friend
   D. Father

11. What is a good posture for prayer? (1 mark)
   A. Eat snacks
   B. Lie down and talk
   C. Jump around
   D. Sit calmly with hands folded

12. What does vidya mean in the prayer? (1 mark)
   A. Friend
   B. Knowledge
   C. Father
   D. Wealth

13. What is the benefit of Sasankasana? (1 mark)
   A. It makes the arms shorter
   B. It stretches the back and shoulders and relaxes
   C. It cures every disease
   D. It is useless

14. What does karma mean? (1 mark)
   A. Action
   B. Water
   C. Wealth
   D. Prayer

15. Which of these is a way of following Artha? (1 mark)
   A. Wasting food
   B. Cheating
   C. Saving pocket money and not taking what is not yours
   D. Stealing

16. According to the teaching, what happens to good actions? (1 mark)
   A. They bring bad luck
   B. They are forgotten
   C. They bring good results
   D. They have no results

17. Which important idea about the Purusharthas is taught? (1 mark)
   A. Wishes come first
   B. Wealth is all that matters
   C. Ignore Dharma
   D. Balance, with wealth and wishes following Dharma

18. In which months of the usual calendar does Maha Shivratri usually fall? (1 mark)
   A. December or January
   B. October or November
   C. July or August
   D. February or March

19. Which of these is NOT true about the flag? (1 mark)
   A. It is a national symbol
   B. It should be respected
   C. It is raised at ceremonies
   D. It may touch the ground

20. What is patriotism? (1 mark)
   A. Love for one's country
   B. Dislike of others
   C. Love for sweets
   D. Fear of others

21. Which national symbol is raised at Madaraka Day ceremonies? (1 mark)
   A. A flag of a sports team
   B. The national flag
   C. The school flag
   D. A sail

22. Which festival comes first in the year in the lesson's timeline? (1 mark)
   A. Jamhuri Day
   B. Madaraka Day
   C. Maha Shivratri
   D. Paryushan

23. What does the Kiswahili word Madaraka mean? (1 mark)
   A. Freedom of religion
   B. Food
   C. Peace
   D. Power or authority to govern

24. Which Jain scripture is often read during Paryushan? (1 mark)
   A. Kalpasutra
   B. Dhammapada
   C. Guru Granth Sahib
   D. Ramayan

25. Som is another name for which heavenly body? (1 mark)
   A. The Sun
   B. Saturn
   C. Jupiter
   D. The Moon

26. How many months are in the Indian traditional calendar year? (1 mark)
   A. Twelve
   B. Ten
   C. Fifteen
   D. Seven

27. Guru (Brihaspati) is the Indian name for which planet? (1 mark)
   A. Jupiter
   B. Venus
   C. Mars
   D. Saturn

28. Which is a use of the Panchang? (1 mark)
   A. Cooking rice
   B. Keeping the school timetable
   C. Fixing the dates of festivals
   D. Counting rainfall

29. What does graha mean in this tradition? (1 mark)
   A. A heavenly body
   B. A river
   C. A festival
   D. A house

30. Which is a memory trick for the seven names? (1 mark)
   A. Skipping them
   B. Writing them once
   C. Making a rhyme or song
   D. Reading backwards only

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. How can you learn more about the scriptures? Give four ways. (4 marks)

32. State three contributions of Sri Guru Ram Das Ji. (3 marks)

33. Explain how the days of the week are related to the solar system. (3 marks)

34. Explain why forgiveness is important, using Paryushan Parva. (4 marks)

35. List three things you should do before starting yoga. (3 marks)

36. Explain the Sikh idea of Kirat Karni. (2 marks)

37. Explain how to say the Gayatri Mantra correctly. (3 marks)

38. Describe the snake story of Lord Parshvanath. (3 marks)

39. What is a festival? (2 marks)

40. Explain why respect for the holy books of other faiths is important in Kenya. (5 marks)

41. Match the days to the heavenly bodies: Ravivaar, Somvaar, Mangalvaar. (3 marks)

42. Describe how a child can follow all five principles in one day. (5 marks)

43. State two reasons why trees and plants are important. (2 marks)

44. Describe what Prince Siddhartha did when a swan was hurt. (3 marks)

45. Tell the story of Prahlad and Hiranyakashipu in three sentences. (3 marks)

46. Explain the meaning of the word Paramatma. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — MOCK EXAM #3 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Life cannot continue without it
   People, animals and plants all need water to live.

2. D — Satya, always speak the truth
   Satya means truthfulness.

3. A — With cleanliness and respect
   Scriptures are kept clean and high.

4. C — Uttaradhyayan Sutra
   It teaches Ahimsa, truth and control of anger.

5. D — Sage Valmiki
   Valmiki is honoured as its author.

6. B — Keep your promises
   Ram kept his father's promise.

7. C — Slowly and clearly, sitting quietly
   Calm and clear.

8. A — Modestly
   Modest dress shows respect.

9. B — A safe digital map with a teacher's help
   We can use a map on a tablet.

10. D — Father
   Pita means father.

11. D — Sit calmly with hands folded
   Calm sitting is respectful.

12. B — Knowledge
   Vidya is knowledge.

13. B — It stretches the back and shoulders and relaxes
   It gently stretches and relaxes.

14. A — Action
   Karma is action and its results.

15. C — Saving pocket money and not taking what is not yours
   Artha is honest wealth.

16. C — They bring good results
   Good actions bring good results.

17. D — Balance, with wealth and wishes following Dharma
   Dharma guides the others.

18. D — February or March
   Phalguna usually falls then.

19. D — It may touch the ground
   The flag should never touch the ground.

20. A — Love for one's country
   Patriotism is love for our country.

21. B — The national flag
   The flag is raised and the anthem sung.

22. C — Maha Shivratri
   It is in February or March.

23. D — Power or authority to govern
   It means authority to govern.

24. A — Kalpasutra
   Many Jains hear the Kalpasutra.

25. D — The Moon
   Som is the Moon.

26. A — Twelve
   It has twelve months.

27. A — Jupiter
   Guru is Jupiter.

28. C — Fixing the dates of festivals
   It lists festival dates.

29. A — A heavenly body
   Graha is a heavenly body.

30. C — Making a rhyme or song
   Songs help us remember.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: Listen to a resource person, visit a temple or library, discuss with friends, watch a documentary, use a safe search engine with an adult (any four).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: He started the city of Amritsar and the Sarovar, composed hymns and the Laavan, and taught equality and service.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each contribution.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: They are named after the Sun, the Moon and five planets that people could see in the sky, so each day has a heavenly partner.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for Sun and Moon, planets and naming.

34. (4 marks)
   Answer: Forgiveness removes anger, mends friendships and brings peace. On the last day Jains ask everyone for forgiveness with Micchami Dukkadam.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four points.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: Wear loose clothes, prepare a mat, have an empty stomach, find a quiet place, meet with a teacher (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

36. (2 marks)
   Answer: Earning a living by honest work.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for earning and 1 mark for honest work.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sit quietly with a straight back, close eyes and breathe slowly, say it one line at a time and listen first to a teacher or recording so you copy the sounds.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for three points.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: A man was burning a log. Parshvanath saw that a snake was inside and asked him to stop. The snake was saved, and the man learned a lesson about kindness.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the log, 1 mark for the snake, 1 mark for the rescue or lesson.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: A special day or set of days when people come together to remember something important.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for special day and 1 mark for remembering or celebrating together.

40. (5 marks)
   Answer: Kenya has people of many faiths, and respect helps us live in peace and unity. Making fun of another's holy book hurts feelings and causes conflict. Listening and learning builds understanding.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for many faiths, 1 mark for peace and unity, 1 mark for hurt feelings, 1 mark for learning, 1 mark for a clear example.

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sun, Moon, Mars.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.

42. (5 marks)
   Answer: Morning prayer and Namaste (Prarthana, Paramatma), honest schoolwork (Dharma, Artha), helping a friend (Prani Daya), thinking about the day's good deeds (Punarjanam and karma).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each principle applied, up to 5.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: They give oxygen, shade, food and medicine; their leaves are used in worship (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid reason.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: He pulled out the arrow, nursed the swan and, when it was well, let it go free. He said that saving a life matters more than taking it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for nursing, arrow, letting go free.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Hiranyakashipu was a proud king who wanted to be called God. His young son Prahlad kept praying to Vishnu. Lord Narsimha appeared from a pillar and defeated the king.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the proud king, 1 mark for Prahlad's faith, 1 mark for Narsimha.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: The Supreme Soul, or God.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each.
